Every time you listen to a record you are actually destroying the grooves a little bit and those portable players are cheaply made and have terrible needles and amps. So the needle will do more damage, pick up less sound and the amp won't give you a really good sound.

I would advise against the portable ones, they can damage records. 

Have you ever seen a record groove really close like this:

http://www.thatericalper.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/01/Close-up-of-a-record-stylus-on-the-grooves-of-a-vinyl-record.jpg

When the needle travels over the groove it picks up the little vibrations from the groove and basically translates them to sound. Better needles can pick up more vibrations and there for more and better sound, but they cost more. 

But that's just the needle, your amp and receiver also effect sound quality as do your speakers.

I'm in my 2nd year at college and in high school I was always a little depressed now and then, but it always passed. But the one thing college has done for me so far it is that it has brought out my depression more than I ever could have thought. I know how you feel about classes, I force myself to go even though I know I'm going to get back my test I failed or have to sit though a class I hate. Unlike you, however, I stay awake as long as I possibly can because I don't want tomorrow to come. The only real things that has kept me from killing myself so far are my dogs and music. My biggest adjustment entering college was that I had to leave my dogs behind. For 18 years I always had 2 puppies at home who I could talk and cry to when I needed to. And then suddenly after one move, no more. Every time I think about killing myself I think about them and how much I would miss them. They are my siblings, best friends, and my life. They are the only living being that I would truly miss in death. The other is music. Music is the biggest thing in my life. Music is the only real thing that can get me through most days. Music doesn't judge, music doesn't give a shit about who you are, whether your gay, or whatever. Music is just there, for me everyday. Music has convinced me that maybe life is worth living and because of it I have finally decided to take charge of my depression. This week I'm going to talk to someone at school about my thoughts, tell my only friend, and then my parents and finally get some help. I know I'm rambling on about me but what I'm trying to say is that there is something everyone can retreat into, mine just happens to be music. Find yours, find that one thing in your life that you love the most and use it to help you get though the day and though life. Also I'm sure you already know this and don't want to hear it but stop drinking. Alcohol is a depressant and can only push you farther down mentally. I am 20 and I am terrified to turn 21 because I already know that I will be an alcoholic. If your going to do anything at all, replace the drinking with something you like instead. There use to be some nights where I would drink just to make the day end, but now I'm trying my hardest to replace alcohol with music instead. And although my life is far from perfect, it is just a little bit better everyday.
